parts: #If I were to estimate ChiSq using the model and observed cov matrices

S <- cov(d); S

Note that in accordance with asymptotic theory, lavaan rescales this sample covariance to divide the sum of squares and cross-products by N rather than N - 1, unless you override the default by setting sample.cov.rescale=FALSE (see ?lavOptions).

Random tip:  you can print when assigning by doing so within parentheses:

(S <- cov(d))

#Without scaling of number of observation, Fit function
fitf <- log(det(C)) - log(det(S)) + sum(diag(S %*% solve(C))) - n

Yes, although you are missing a term for the mean structure (if your model has a non-saturated mean structure)

Note that this is the average -2*log(likelihood-ratio)s comparing your fitted model to a saturated model.  Multiplying a mean by N gives the sum of casewise -2*log(likelihood-ratio)s, which is distributed as a chi-squared random variable.
likl = log(det(C)) + sum(diag(S%*%solve(C))) - log(det(S)) - n
No, the fit function does not return the log(likelihood) of the fitted model.  That can be found with logLik(fit)

bic = -2*log(likl) + log(N)*((count_free_parameters(fit1) - (nfac == 0, 1,0))
Error: unexpected ',' in "bic = -2*log(likl) + log(N)*((count_free_parameters(fit1) - (nfac == 0,"

As the error message indicates, there is a problematic comma. What do you mean to do with this bit of syntax?

- (nfac == 0, 1,0)

Did you mean to use the ifelse() function with that test of nfac==0, returning a dummy code?

 chisq = likl*(N-1)

Note also that lavaan multiplies the fit function by N, in accordance with asymptotic normal theory, unless you override the default by setting likelihood="wishart"

I suspect if you multiply your S by (N-1)/N, and multiply your fit function by N, then your results should match lavaan's chi-squared.  If you have a follow-up, please use/adapt a help-page example so we can also run your syntax.
